learning_outcomes.text: Possess the ability to design, develop, implement, manage and improve products, systems and processes in different industrial fields, using appropriate analytical, computational or experimental techniques.
Apply acquired knowledge to identify, formulate and solve problems in broad contexts, being able to integrate them while working in multidisciplinary teams.
Understand the impact of engineering on the environment, the sustainable development of society and the importance of working in a professional and responsible environment.
Possess learning skills that allow continuous lifelong learning for adequate professional development.
Incorporate ICT and Industrial Engineering technologies and tools into their professional activities.
Organization and planning of projects and human teams. Teamwork and leadership skills.
Applied knowledge of manufacturing systems and processes, metrology and quality control.
Knowledge and practical application of automated programming of machine tools equipped with numerical control systems in CAD/CAM environments.

syllabus_topics: Characteristics of Numerical Control Machine Tools
Introduction to automated quality control centers
Characteristics of milling and drilling tools
Selection of machining parameters and tools
Manual programming of NC milling machine
Basic programming of milling machines with numerical control
Advanced programming of milling machines with numerical control
Parametric programming of milling machines with numerical control
Automatic programming of NC milling machine
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, progressive evaluation leads to a final grade (NMC) calculated as 0.30·CPF + 0.25·CPP + 0.45·CPO. To pass this path, students must attend mandatory lab practices, complete the mandatory Fabrication Project, score at least 4/10 in each Progressive Test (PP1 & PP2), score at least 4/10 in the combined practical computer tests (CPO), and achieve an overall NMC of 5/10 or higher. If progressive evaluation requirements are not met, students enter a global evaluation path, where previously passed progressive test scores are retained, and remaining parts are recovered. The NMC for global evaluation is 0.30·CPF + 0.125·CPG1 + 0.125·CPG2 + 0.45·CPO, requiring mandatory lab attendance, completion of the Fabrication Project, a minimum of 4/10 in CPO, and an overall NMC of 5/10 or higher. For the extraordinary call, a single final written and computer-based exam accounts for 100% of the final grade, requiring mandatory lab attendance and a minimum of 5/10 on the exam to pass.
